ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=\frac{1}{2}x$ intersects the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}\ (x>0)$ at point $A(4, m)$, and point $B(n, 2n)$ is another point on the graph of the inverse proportion function. The line AB intersects the x-axis at point C. Find the analytical expression of the inverse proportion function and the coordinates of point B?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the line $y=\frac{1}{2}x$ intersects the graph of the inverse proportionality function $y=\frac{k}{x}\left(x>0\right)$ at point $A\left(4, m\right)$,\\
then $m=\frac{1}{2}\times 4=2$,\\
thus the coordinates of point A are $\left(4, 2\right)$,\\
thereby $k=2\times 4=8$,\\
hence the equation of the inverse proportionality function is: $y=\frac{8}{x}$,\\
Given that point $B\left(n, 2n\right)$ lies on the graph of the inverse proportionality function,\\
thus $2n=\frac{8}{n}$,\\
solving this gives: $n_{1}=2$, $n_{2}=-2$ (discard),\\
upon verification, these are the roots of the equation\\
therefore, the coordinates of point B are $\boxed{\left(2, 4\right)}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The line $y=\frac{1}{2}x$ intersects the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ $(x>0)$ at point $A(4,m)$, and point $B(n,2n)$ is another point on the graph of the inverse proportion function. The line $AB$ intersects the x-axis at point $C$. Find the analytical expression of the inverse proportion function and the coordinates of point $B$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, with the x-axis pointing to the right and the y-axis pointing upward; in the first quadrant there is drawn an inverse proportional function curve. Point A is located at the intersection of the inverse proportional curve and a straight line passing through the origin with positive slope; point B is a point on the same inverse proportional curve that is farther to the upper left. The straight line passing through A and B extends toward the lower right and intersects the x-axis at point C. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, A=(4,m) is on the straight line y=\frac12 x, so m=\frac12\cdot 4=2, that is, A=(4,2). Also A is on the inverse proportional function y=\frac{k}{x}; substituting gives 2=\frac{k}{4}, so k=8. Therefore the inverse proportional function is y=\frac{8}{x}. Point B=(n,2n) is also on the graph of this function, so 2n=\frac{8}{n}. Because the domain of the function gives x>0, therefore n>0; thus 2n^2=8, n^2=4, n=2. Substituting back into B=(n,2n), we get B=(2,4).
